verifications.claim: NASA’s Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026 Artemis II lifts off'; R2: 'blasted off ... on Wednesday evening ... April 1'; R3: 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm successful launch on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: NASA’s Artemis II mission launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R2: 'at 6:35 p.m. Eastern time'; R3: 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and timezone directly stated in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: NASA’s Artemis II mission launched from Kennedy Space Center, Florida
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R2: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R3: 'Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly state launch site as Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket carried four astronauts into orbit
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis II SLS ... rocket, with'; R3: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS ... rocket ... carrying NASA astronauts ... lifted off'; R6: 'Artemis II SLS ... rocket with the Orion spacecraft launches'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SLS rocket launched with Orion carrying four astronauts into orbit.

verifications.claim: NASA’s Artemis II mission is the first crewed mission to the moon in over 50 years
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R2: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'; R4: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe it as first crewed lunar mission since Apollo (over 50 years).

verifications.claim: NASA’s Artemis II mission is aimed at a 10-day journey around the lunar surface
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'about nine and a half days ... loop around it'; R3: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon'; R4: '10 days in space, orbiting the Earth once before flying to the moon, around it'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm ~10-day mission looping/flying around the moon; 'lunar surface' aligns with descriptions of viewing/flying around it.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed moon flyby since Apollo
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program'; R2: 'equivalent of Apollo 8 ... first time humans reached another celestial body'
verifications.reasoning: Sources position it as first crewed lunar mission/flyby since Apollo era.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; identical in others
verifications.reasoning: All sources list exact crew names matching the claim.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II is in high Earth orbit following a successful liftoff
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'highly elliptical 24-hour-long orbit ... apogee ... 43,760 miles'; R2: 'high-Earth orbit'; R3: 'high Earth orbit ahead of a proximity operations demonstration'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm crew in high Earth orbit post-liftoff.

verifications.claim: The goal of Artemis II is a 10-day mission to orbit the moon and return to Earth
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead, the plan is to loop around it'; R2: 'around the moon but not land there'; R3: 'around the Moon and back'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state no lunar orbit; it's a flyby/loop around the moon, contradicting 'orbit the moon'.

verifications.claim: There were minor reports of issues with the toilet system onboard Artemis II
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Issue with toilet being worked on ... "controller issue" with the toilet'; R2: 'undisclosed problem with the spacecraft’s toilet'; R5: 'broken toilet ... teething issues with the Orion spacecraft's toilet'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources report minor toilet controller issue post-launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is proceeding
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II crew begins first day in space after exhilarating launch'; R4: 'Artemis II mission are on their way'; R5: 'Orion is on its way ... mission was able to successfully execute'
verifications.reasoning: All post-launch sources confirm mission proceeding successfully.
